newsitem.title: INDIA: India's Miss World protesters to take cyanide.
newsitem.headline: India's Miss World protesters to take cyanide.

text.p: An Indian group threatening mass suicide in protest against the Miss World beauty pageant said on Friday its members would take cyanide pills to dull the agony of setting themselves on fire.
"Many are worried about the agony of burning. We will each have a cyanide pill to escape the agony," K.N. Shashikala, the group's leader, told Reuters.

But J.H. Patel, chief minister of the Karnataka state in which much of the pageant is due to take place, said tight security arrangements at the stadium would frustrate the plans of Mahila Jagran Samiti (Forum for the Awakening of Women).
"It is an empty threat," he said. "Police will take care of those elements. The show will go on."

Bangalore police plan a massive security operation involving more than 12,000 officers to safeguard the November 23 event, which drew an estimated television audience of two billion viewers last year.
The contest has drawn fire since one of India's most popular film stars, Amitabh Bachchan, announced he had secured the rights to hold it India for the first time.

Shashikala said the group had abandoned earlier plans to have one member per day set herself on fire, saying they wanted to preserve their 15-strong suicide squad for the final event, the crowning ceremony, Shashikala said.
"We have to live to thwart the final event," she said. "We will sneak into the stadium and burn ourselves. We have already bought tickets," she said.

It has also been hotly opposed by the Hindu nationalist Bharatiya Janata Party as well as the State Farmers' Association, which has attacked the American fast-food outlet Kentucky Fried Chicken and other Western multinational firms.
The protests prompted the organisers to shift the pageant's swimsuit competition to the Indian Ocean's Seychelles islands.
Shashikala said she feared events like the Miss World contest would increase promiscuity and prostitution.
"Visitors from India and abroad will lure minor girls into prostitution," she said. "It will definitely affect our culture. Wearing mini-skirts is not part of our traditional culture."
After Shashikala's group sought to ban the contest, a Bangalore court on Thursday ordered the state government not to assist the pageant in any way apart from providing security.
